result.finding: Assessed 6 CWE rules in Concurrency & Synchronization: 4 FOUND, 2 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Scanned application source files for concurrency & synchronization patterns

values.name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
values.description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.

evidence.explanation: ApplicationModule.Load registers CatalogServiceMock as .SingleInstance() at lines 18-22, making one shared service instance for all requests. CatalogServiceMock stores mutable shared state in the catalogItems list at lines 12-17 and mutates it in CreateCatalogItem/UpdateCatalogItem/RemoveCatalogItem without synchronization, creating a singleton-in-multithreaded-context risk.

values.name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
values.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

evidence.explanation: CatalogServiceMock keeps a shared List<CatalogItem> in the catalogItems field (lines 12-17). Methods GetCatalogItemsPaginated, FindCatalogItem, CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem, and RemoveCatalogItem access and mutate that shared list at lines 19-67 with no locking or thread-safe collection, allowing concurrent reads/writes across ASP.NET requests.

values.name: Improper Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.

evidence.explanation: CatalogServiceMock performs non-atomic multi-step operations on the shared catalogItems list, such as computing Max(i => i.Id) then adding a new item in CreateCatalogItem (lines 48-53), and finding then replacing an item in UpdateCatalogItem (lines 55-61), without synchronization. Concurrent execution can race and corrupt state or duplicate IDs.

values.name: Improper Locking
values.description: The product does not properly acquire or release a lock on a resource, leading to unexpected resource state changes and behaviors.

values.name: Missing Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.

evidence.explanation: ApplicationModule makes CatalogServiceMock a shared singleton at lines 18-22, while CatalogServiceMock accesses the shared catalogItems list at lines 19-67 with no lock, Monitor, Mutex, Semaphore, or other synchronization primitive. This is a direct missing-synchronization pattern for concurrent request handling.

values.name: Incorrect Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner, but it does not correctly synchronize access to the resource.
